title: From Missteps to Mastery: Enhancing Low-Resource Dense Retrieval through Adaptive Query Generation

problem.claim: Dense retrieval depends on extensive annotated document-query pairs, limiting competitiveness in low-resource scenarios.

gap.claim: Existing few-shot LLM and prompt-engineering approaches for synthetic data generation are hindered by lower-quality data in conventional dense retrieval training.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces iGFT, a low-resource dense-retrieval framework combining Generation, Filtering, and Tuning with iterative optimization.
The framework uses supervised fine-tuning on limited ground-truth data to make an LLM generate candidate queries from documents.
The framework includes multi-stage filtering and an iterative optimization strategy to reduce generated-data noise and produce more informative queries.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly distinguish iGFT as a newly introduced framework and describe the iterative optimization strategy as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on publicly available retrieval benchmark datasets demonstrated iGFT's effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Document retrieval supports information-seeking tasks, and dense retrieval has improved semantic matching over sparse methods.
Dependence on annotated pairs creates a low-resource limitation, while synthetic-data approaches suffer from lower-quality generated data.
iGFT addresses the limitation through generation, filtering, tuning, and iterative optimization.
The authors report effectiveness on publicly available retrieval benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: Synthetic queries can be generated from documents by an LLM fine-tuned on limited ground-truth data.

interpretation.claim: A small supervised seed can initialize data generation for low-resource retrieval.

application.claim: Use limited labeled data to bootstrap document-to-query generation when annotated pairs are scarce.

exception.claim: Generated data may introduce noise and require filtering before retrieval-model tuning.

source_observation.claim: The query generator is iteratively optimized to produce more informative queries.

interpretation.claim: Feedback from downstream retrieval tuning can guide improvement of synthetic-query generation.

application.claim: Consider iterative generator refinement rather than a single synthetic-data generation pass.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the optimization signals or conditions under which iteration is beneficial.

unknowns: Benchmark dataset identities, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The filtering criteria, iterative optimization objective, and training details are not specified.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational cost, or failure cases.
